title: Latency-aware hedging + capacity-weighted geo-pinning for multi-region routing
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Design and implement a multi-region routing policy that balances latency-based hedging, soft geo-pinning, and capacity-weighted steering to meet P99 latency SLOs while avoiding cascading failures. This ticket captures the implementation plan, control knobs, rollout steps, and validation for a first-pass production rollout. Key ideas: 1) latency hedging with short probe requests to alternate regions under tail latency spikes; 2) soft geo-pinning that prefers local region but allows traffic spill with hysteresis and user affinity cookie; 3) capacity-aware steering using region capacity slots and proportional weights, with circuit breakers that trip based on burn-rate-adjusted error/latency signals; 4) graceful load shedding strategies (shorten generation length, prefer smaller model variant, return cached summaries) when region capacity is saturated.
acceptance_criteria: P99 end-to-end latency for routed requests stays within SLO bounds (<= 400ms for text-gen small seqs) across 95% of synthetic traffic profiles used in perf harness
Hedging reduces tail latency regressions in at least 3 of 4 tested failure scenarios (regional saturation, kernel OOM, sporadic network loss, cold-cache spikes)
Soft geo-pinning honors user affinity 95% of the time for steady-state traffic but allows controlled spill when region capacity < 20% of target
Capacity-aware steering reacts within 10s to region capacity changes and rebalances weights without oscillation (validated by a canary traffic test)
Circuit breaker correctly opens for a region when latency/error burn rate crosses threshold and auto-closes after successful recovery window, with all events logged to Console alerts
Load-shedding policies trigger gracefully under overload and produce acceptably degraded outputs (shorter completions, model fallback) with <1% user-visible errors for canary customers
tasks: Finalize routing policy RFC and attach knob matrix (latency probe timeout, hedging threshold, pinning hysteresis, capacity weight floor)
Implement hedging plumbing in request router: parallel short-probe path + cancellation semantics
Add region capacity telemetry (available slots, inflight tokens) and expose via routing API
Implement soft geo-pinning: user-affinity cookie + pin expiry + controlled spillover rules
Circuit breaker: implement burn-rate calculation (error+latency), trip logic, and integration with load-shed actions
Load shedding strategies: short-gen, model-variant fallback, cached-response layer integration
Add end-to-end integration tests in perf-harness and run chaos scenarios (loss, OOM, saturate GPUs)
Create Console dashboards + alerts: per-region SLO burn, hedging rate, CB trips, capacity floor events
Run staged rollout: internal dogfood -> select canary customers -> general availability

notes: Trade-offs: hedging improves P99 but increases upstream cost and risk of double inference; mitigations include hedging budget per-customer, probe-only hedges for short requests, and conservative hedging rate during peak. Soft geo-pinning preserves compliance with a user-affinity token; strict pinning remains an option behind tenant flags. Circuit breaker burn-rate uses combined latency and error signals to be sensitive to both service degradation and functional failures. Next steps: complete perf-harness scenarios, land PRs for hedging + capacity telemetry, and schedule canary cohort with two enterprise customers.
